text.title: Tech futures rise as Nvidia eases AI worries; Waller floats half-point hike
text.summary: Futures are mixed: Nasdaq 100 is up 0.5% and S&P 500 up 0.2%, while Dow futures are down 0.2% and Russell 2000 futures down 0.4%. That follows Tuesday's selloff, when the S&P 500 fell 1.0% and the Dow 1.6%. Gold is down 2.8% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.9%, with no single clear driver in the headlines.

drivers.t: Nvidia shares rose in extended trading after an earnings beat and solid outlook, its first report since CEO Jensen Huang resigned. Bloomberg says this halted a dayslong tech selloff.

Fed governor Christopher Waller said the Fed may need to consider a half-point rate hike because inflation is heading the wrong way. The 10-year yield is 5.10% (down 2 bp) and the 2-year is 4.80% (down 3 bp) as of Tuesday's close.
Mortgage rates hit their highest in three weeks last week, and demand for both refinancing and home purchase loans fell.

ECB Vice President Boris Vujcic said a December rate hike looks 'very likely', with more possible in 2027. Europe is slightly lower: the FTSE 100 is down 0.5%, the DAX down 0.3% and the Euro Stoxx 50 down 0.1%.
The IEA chief said the Iran war has 'crushed' confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable corridor. WTI crude is little changed at $84.29 (down 0.4%).

earnings.t: Target posted its best sales growth in five years and raised guidance, though the stock is down 1.2% pre-market.
Lowe's cited strong online sales and raised its full-year outlook despite a slow housing market, yet the stock is down 4.0% pre-market.
Nvidia's report was its first since Huang's resignation, and interim CEO Colette Kress's first earnings call.

watch: FOMC meeting minutes at 2:00 PM ET (high impact).
Anthropic's IPO is set to price today.
APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen for talks on trade and security, with President Trump attending.
